# Standard deviation - Practice Test - Year 10A

Attempt all questions and show your working. Suggested time: 30 to 35 minutes. Unless a question says otherwise, use the population standard deviation ($\sigma$, often shown as $\sigma_x$ on a calculator), and round standard deviations that are not exact to two decimal places.

## Section A: Consolidating (Questions 1-4)

**Question 1**

Ava recorded the number of emails she received on five days: 12, 7, 15, 9, 17.

(a) Find the mean.

(b) Find the range.

**Question 2**

The data set 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9 has a mean of $\bar{x} = 5$.

(a) Copy and complete the table.

| $x$ | 2 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 7 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $x - \bar{x}$ | $-3$ | $\Box$ | $\Box$ | $\Box$ | $\Box$ | $\Box$ | $\Box$ | $\Box$ |
| $(x - \bar{x})^{2}$ | 9 | $\Box$ | $\Box$ | $\Box$ | $\Box$ | $\Box$ | $\Box$ | $\Box$ |

(b) Find the sum of the squared deviations.

(c) Find the standard deviation using $\sigma = \sqrt{\dfrac{\text{sum of squared deviations}}{n}}$.

**Question 3**

Two sets of data both have a mean of 50.

Set A: 48, 50, 50, 52, 50

Set B: 30, 70, 40, 60, 50

Without calculating, which set has the larger standard deviation? Explain.

**Question 4**

The number of pets in 20 households is shown.

| Number of pets | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 4 | 7 | 5 | 3 | 1 |

Find the mean number of pets per household.

## Section B: Standard (Questions 5-16)

**Question 5**

A netball team scored these numbers of goals in six games: 45, 46, 48, 49, 52, 60.

(a) Find the mean.

(b) Find the standard deviation.

(c) In how many games was the score within one standard deviation of the mean? (Count a score exactly one standard deviation away as within.)

**Question 6**

Two Year 10 classes sat the same test. Both classes had a mean of 68%. Class A had a standard deviation of 4% and Class B had a standard deviation of 12%.

(a) Which class had the more consistent results? Explain.

(b) Describe what the standard deviation of 12% tells you about the results of Class B.

(c) Which class is more likely to include a student who scored above 90%? Explain.

**Question 7**

The daily maximum temperatures in a town over a fortnight had a mean of $20^\circ\text{C}$ and a standard deviation of $3^\circ\text{C}$.

(a) The thermometer was found to read $2^\circ\text{C}$ too low, so 2 degrees is added to every reading. Find the new mean and standard deviation.

(b) Instead, the original readings are converted to degrees Fahrenheit using $F = 1.8C + 32$. Find the mean and standard deviation in degrees Fahrenheit.

(c) Explain why adding the same number to every value does not change the standard deviation.

**Question 8**

Six students recorded their travel times to school in minutes: 10, 11, 14, 16, 17, 22.

(a) Find the mean and standard deviation of the six times.

(b) A seventh student, who lives on a farm, takes 64 minutes. Find the mean and standard deviation of all seven times.

(c) Describe the effect of this one value on the mean and on the standard deviation.

**Question 9**

For data with a symmetric, bell-shaped distribution, about 68% of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95% lie within two standard deviations, and about 99.7% lie within three standard deviations.

The heights of Year 10 students at a large school have this shape, with a mean of 168 cm and a standard deviation of 7 cm.

(a) Between which two heights do about 68% of the students lie?

(b) Between which two heights do about 95% of the students lie?

(c) In a group of 400 of these students, about how many would you expect to be taller than 175 cm?

**Question 10**

Sixteen students sat a quiz marked out of 10.

| Score | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 1 | 4 | 6 | 4 | 1 |

(a) Find the mean score.

(b) Find the standard deviation.

(c) What percentage of the students scored within one standard deviation of the mean? (Count a score exactly one standard deviation away as within.)

**Question 11**

Five values in a data set are 8, 10, 13, $x$ and 15. The mean is 12.

(a) Find $x$.

(b) Find the standard deviation of the five values.

**Question 12**

A data set is 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.

(a) Find the standard deviation.

(b) The value 6 is added to the data set. Find the new standard deviation.

(c) Explain why the standard deviation went down even though no value was removed.

**Question 13**

A standardised score (z-score) shows how many standard deviations a result is above or below the mean: $z = \dfrac{\text{score} - \text{mean}}{\text{standard deviation}}$.

Mia scored 76 in a Maths test (class mean 60, standard deviation 8) and 78 in an English test (class mean 70, standard deviation 5).

(a) Find Mia's z-score for each test.

(b) In which subject did Mia perform better compared with her class? Explain.

(c) What English score would have given Mia the same z-score as her Maths result?

**Question 14**

The maximum temperatures ($^\circ\text{C}$) over the same five days in two towns were:

| Town | Day 1 | Day 2 | Day 3 | Day 4 | Day 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Town P (inland) | 18 | 22 | 24 | 26 | 30 |
| Town Q (coastal) | 21 | 23 | 24 | 25 | 27 |

(a) Find the mean temperature for each town.

(b) Find the standard deviation for each town.

(c) Compare the temperatures in the two towns using your answers.

**Question 15**

Write true or false for each statement.

(a) A standard deviation can be negative.

(b) If every value in a data set is the same, the standard deviation is 0.

(c) The standard deviation has the same units as the data.

(d) Adding an outlier to a data set has no effect on the standard deviation.

(e) Two data sets with the same mean must have the same standard deviation.

**Question 16**

A data set is 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. For each change below (each one made to the original data), say whether the standard deviation increases, decreases or stays the same.

(a) The value 8 is added to the data set.

(b) The value 12 is changed to 20.

(c) 5 is added to every value.

(d) The values 4 and 12 are both changed to 8.

(e) Every value is multiplied by 2.

## Section C: Advanced (Questions 17-20)

**Question 17**

For a data set of $n$ values, the sum of the values is $\Sigma x = n\bar{x}$, the sum of the squares of the values is $\Sigma x^{2} = n(\sigma^{2} + \bar{x}^{2})$, and $\sigma = \sqrt{\dfrac{\Sigma x^{2}}{n} - \bar{x}^{2}}$.

A cricketer's scores in her first 10 innings had a mean of 32 runs and a standard deviation of 10 runs. In her 11th innings she scored 98 runs.

(a) Show that the sum of her first 10 scores is 320.

(b) Show that the sum of the squares of her first 10 scores is 11 240.

(c) Find the mean of all 11 scores.

(d) Find the standard deviation of all 11 scores.

(e) Comment on the effect of the score of 98.

**Question 18**

A science class measured the time (in seconds) for a ball to roll down a ramp, and recorded these eight results: 52, 55, 58, 60, 61, 63, 65, 95.

(a) Find the mean and standard deviation of the recorded results.

(b) The result of 95 was a recording mistake and should have been 59. Find the correct mean and standard deviation.

(c) By how much did the mistake change the mean? Which statistic was affected more by the mistake, compared with its correct value?

**Question 19**

(a) Write a set of four whole numbers with a mean of 10 and a standard deviation of 5.

(b) Show that your set has a standard deviation of 5.

(c) Explain why no set of four numbers with a mean of 10 and every value between 8 and 12 (inclusive) can have a standard deviation of 5.

**Question 20**

Two classes sat the same exam. Class A has 20 students with a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 6. Class B has 30 students with a mean of 80 and a standard deviation of 4.

(a) Find the mean of all 50 students.

(b) Use $\Sigma x^{2} = n(\sigma^{2} + \bar{x}^{2})$ to find the sum of the squares of the scores for each class.

(c) Find the standard deviation of all 50 scores, using $\sigma = \sqrt{\dfrac{\Sigma x^{2}}{n} - \bar{x}^{2}}$.

(d) Explain why the standard deviation for all 50 students is larger than the standard deviation of either class.

# Standard deviation - Answer Key

These answers use the population standard deviation ($\sigma$, dividing by $n$), as the test asks. If your child's calculator gave the sample standard deviation ($s$, dividing by $n - 1$), also accept: Q5(b) $5.48$; Q8 (a) $4.38$, (b) $18.95$; Q10(b) $1.03$; Q11(b) $2.92$; Q12 (a) $3.16$, (b) $2.83$; Q14(b) Town P $4.47$, Town Q $2.24$; Q17(d) $22.27$; Q18 (a) $13.35$, (b) $4.19$; Q20(c) $7.00$. The other parts' answers don't change. Q2 and Q19 use the population formula given in the question.

**Question 1**

Answer: (a) $12$ (b) $10$

**Question 2**

Answer: (a) $x - \bar{x}$: $-1, -1, -1, 0, 0, 2, 4$; $(x - \bar{x})^{2}$: $1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 4, 16$ (b) $32$ (c) $\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{32}{8}} = 2$

**Question 3**

Answer: Set B, because its values are much further from the mean of 50 (Set A's values are all within 2 of the mean).

**Question 4**

Answer: $1.5$ pets ($\frac{30}{20}$)

**Question 5**

Answer: (a) $50$ (b) $5$ (c) $5$ games (scores from 45 to 55: all except 60)

**Question 6**

Answer: (a) Class A, because its standard deviation is smaller, so the results are closer to the mean. (b) Class B's results are much more spread out; a typical result is about 12% away from the mean of 68%. (c) Class B, because its results are more spread out (90% is less than 2 standard deviations above its mean, but more than 5 standard deviations above Class A's mean).

**Question 7**

Answer: (a) mean $22^\circ\text{C}$, standard deviation $3^\circ\text{C}$ (b) mean $68^\circ\text{F}$, standard deviation $5.4^\circ\text{F}$ (c) Every value and the mean move by the same amount, so the distance of each value from the mean (the deviations) does not change.

**Question 8**

Answer: (a) mean $15$ minutes, standard deviation $4$ minutes (b) mean $22$ minutes, standard deviation $17.54$ minutes (c) The mean increases by 7 minutes, but the standard deviation increases far more (from 4 to about 17.5, more than 4 times as large); one outlier has a big effect on the standard deviation.

**Question 9**

Answer: (a) $161 \text{ cm}$ to $175 \text{ cm}$ (b) $154 \text{ cm}$ to $182 \text{ cm}$ (c) about $64$ ($16\%$ of 400, since $\frac{100\% - 68\%}{2} = 16\%$)

**Question 10**

Answer: (a) $8$ (b) $1$ ($\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{16}{16}}$) (c) $87.5\%$ (14 of the 16 students scored 7, 8 or 9)

**Question 11**

Answer: (a) $x = 14$ (b) $2.61$ ($\sigma = \sqrt{6.8}$)

**Question 12**

Answer: (a) $2.83$ ($\sqrt{8}$) (b) $2.58$ ($\sqrt{\frac{40}{6}}$) (c) The new value equals the mean, so the sum of squared deviations stays at 40, but it is now divided by 6 instead of 5, so the standard deviation is smaller.

**Question 13**

Answer: (a) Maths: $z = 2$; English: $z = 1.6$ (b) Maths, because her score was more standard deviations above the class mean. (c) $80$ ($70 + 2 \times 5$)

**Question 14**

Answer: (a) both $24^\circ\text{C}$ (b) Town P: $4^\circ\text{C}$; Town Q: $2^\circ\text{C}$ (c) Both towns had the same mean temperature, but Town Q's temperatures were more consistent (smaller standard deviation); Town P's varied twice as much.

**Question 15**

Answer: (a) false (b) true (c) true (d) false (e) false

**Question 16**

Answer: (a) decreases (b) increases (c) stays the same (d) decreases (e) increases (it doubles)

**Question 17**

Answer: (a) $10 \times 32 = 320$ (b) $10(10^{2} + 32^{2}) = 10 \times 1124 = 11\,240$ (c) $38$ ($\frac{418}{11}$) (d) $21.23$ ($\sqrt{\frac{20\,844}{11} - 38^{2}}$) (e) The single high score raised the mean by 6 runs but more than doubled the standard deviation, so it is an outlier with a large effect on the spread.

**Question 18**

Answer: (a) mean $63.625 \text{ s}$ (accept $63.63$), standard deviation $12.49 \text{ s}$ (b) mean $59.125 \text{ s}$ (accept $59.13$), standard deviation $3.92 \text{ s}$ (c) The mean changed by $4.5 \text{ s}$ ($\frac{36}{8}$). The standard deviation was affected much more: the wrong value made it more than 3 times its correct value, while the mean was only about 8% too high.

**Question 19**

Answer: (a) For example 5, 5, 15, 15 (accept any four whole numbers with a sum of 40 and a sum of squared deviations from 10 equal to 100) (b) For 5, 5, 15, 15: deviations $-5, -5, 5, 5$; $\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{25 + 25 + 25 + 25}{4}} = \sqrt{25} = 5$ (c) Every value would be at most 2 from the mean, so every squared deviation is at most 4 and $\sigma \le \sqrt{4} = 2$, which is less than 5.

**Question 20**

Answer: (a) $76$ ($\frac{20 \times 70 + 30 \times 80}{50} = \frac{3800}{50}$) (b) Class A: $98\,720$; Class B: $192\,480$ (c) $6.93$ ($\sqrt{\frac{291\,200}{50} - 76^{2}} = \sqrt{48}$) (d) The two class means (70 and 80) are different, so when the classes are combined the scores are spread around the overall mean of 76 more than each class is spread around its own mean.
check_notes: Every mean and population standard deviation recomputed with Python statistics.pstdev and fractions, including outlier, frequency-table, combined-group and sum-of-squares calculations; true/false and effect questions checked by recomputing each changed data set.
